nchsNatality

Read and losslessly pack NCHS natality public-use files.

The NCHS natality public-use file is a fixed-width text file — one record per birth, no delimiters, no quoting. That defeats delimiter-sniffing readers such as data.table::fread(). nchsNatality reads the file by byte position from the official record layout, optionally converts it to compact, lossless sharded Parquet (via DuckDB), and round-trips it back to fixed-width for verification.

Installation 

# from GitHub
remotes::install_github("vjcitn/nchsNatality")

# or from a local source checkout
devtools::install("path/to/nchsNatality")

Runtime dependencies: data.table, vroom.
Parquet functions additionally require duckdb >= 1.1.0 and DBI.

Quick start 

library(nchsNatality)

f <- "Nat2025PublicUS.c20260624.r20260922.txt"

# 1. Sanity-check the file
check_natality_file(f)
#> terminator: CRLF; record length(s) in first 100000 bytes: 1345
#> (guide documents 1330); '"' bytes: 0

# 2. Read selected fields into a data.table
dt <- read_natality(f, cols = c("MAGER", "DBWT", "COMBGEST", "SEX", "DOB_MM"))

# 3. Attach value labels (turns character codes into factors)
dt <- label_natality(dt)

# 4. Pack to sharded Parquet (requires duckdb)
natality_pack(f, out_dir = "nat_parquet/")
#> Packing 12 shards (DOB_MM 01–12) …
#> Verifying … OK

# 5. Query the Parquet directly with duckdb (no unpacking needed)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE VIEW nat AS SELECT * FROM 'nat_parquet/*.parquet'")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT SEX, COUNT(*) n FROM nat GROUP BY SEX")

# 6. Unpack to a fresh fixed-width file
natality_unpack("nat_parquet/", "Nat2025_copy.txt")

Functions

Function Purpose
check_natality_file() Report line endings and record length
diagnose_layout() Check documented field positions against the file
read_natality() Read fields into a data.table, typed or raw
label_natality() Convert categorical codes to labelled factors
natality_pack() Write sharded Parquet; optionally verify losslessness
natality_verify() Verify an existing Parquet directory against the source file
natality_unpack() Reconstruct the fixed-width file from Parquet
natality_layout() Return the record layout as a data.table
natality_values() Return value labels as a data.table
natality_years() List years for which a layout is bundled

Record-layout notes (2025 file)

The User Guide documents a 1330-byte record. The 2025 public release (Nat2025PublicUS.c20260624.r20260922.txt) has 1345-byte records with CRLF line endings; bytes 1331–1345 are beyond the documented layout. check_natality_file() reports this automatically. natality_pack() detects the actual record length and keeps the extra bytes as a trailing FILLER_1331 column, so no data are lost.

The guide has a few typographic errors; data-raw/parse_userguide.py lists all corrections made when the layout and value-label CSVs were generated.

GitHub size limits

One year of sharded Parquet at compression level 22 is roughly 500 MB to 1 GB (actual size depends on data). That is too large for a GitHub repository (100 MiB hard limit per file; 1 GB soft limit per repo). Options:

  • GitHub Releases – release assets can be up to 2 GB each.
  • Git LFS – transparent large-file storage; free tier 1 GB.
  • Zenodo / OSF / AWS S3 – for public archival distribution.

Legal

The NCHS natality public-use file is a US government work. Review the NCHS data-use agreement before redistributing any derived file.
